submitter: bugfix_282_validate_accepts_menu lane (session bddf9352) — bugs_open/282, validate's resolver drops planner-placed tool sections
rationale:
WHAT IS BROKEN. A planner agent is SHOWN a component menu (build-site-planner's `load_components` step -> the `available_components` array its prompt renders) and `validate_site_plan` then RESOLVES every proposed section name, DROPPING what it cannot resolve (`loadComponentNameResolver`, v3_site_actions.go, `component_level IN ('section','element')` hardcoded). Those are two halves of ONE contract — what may be OFFERED and what will be ACCEPTED — maintained in two places in two languages. Migration 407 (PLAN-049) widened the OFFER to a site's own tool-level components behind a per-site flag; nothing widened the ACCEPTANCE. The planner placed twelve calculators and validate ate all twelve, silently: no error, one Warn per dropped name, and a persisted plan describing twelve calculator pages with no calculators.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (live DB, 2026-08-16, run corr 2f74a975-1a87-40a8-af88-a9bd2ecc1510, plan dcbae4df, loancalculator.co.uk): collected_data.available_components = 151 rows INCLUDING 11 finance tool functions (the planner WAS offered them); collected_data.llm_plan.result names a tool function on 12 pages (index: ["hero","tool-loan-repayment",...]); collected_data.validate_plan — validate's OWN output field — carries NONE of them (index: 5 sections). The drop is inside the action, upstream of write_site_plan. Nothing live was damaged: the tool-role review gate plus 12 permanent locks held. The loancalculator lane's D2 batch (11 owned_page_review + needs_page:index) has been held since 2026-08-15 waiting on this.

THE FIX, IN ONE SENTENCE: the acceptance surface consumes the OFFER'S OUTPUT — the very rows the planner was shown, already in CollectedData — instead of re-deriving the offer's predicate.

WHY NOT MIRROR THE PREDICATE (the bug file's own preferred candidate, rejected on evidence). The menu is not Go: it is a SQL string in agent_definitions.default_config, and it has ALREADY drifted past the text the bug file assumed — migration 419 (bugs_open/276 family, 2026-08-15) added a `requires-backend` clause to that same query and guards its apply by asserting 407's exact bytes as expected_pre. A Go mirror would be a THIRD hand-maintained copy across the SQL/Go line: precisely the idx_swi_dedup <-> workItemTerminalStatuses lockstep class, whose catalogued verdict is 'single-sourcing is a guarantee, a lockstep test is a backstop' (016b s9). Consuming the menu's output single-sources it: any future gate on the menu flows through with nothing to keep in step.

UNION, NOT INTERSECTION. addMenu ADDS the menu's components to the section/element base and never removes, so no site's plan loses a name it accepts today. Intersection (also dropping names the menu WITHHELD — e.g. a requires-backend component on a static site) would close a symmetric hole for the 276 class but is a TIGHTENING on every site on the estate; it is named here as deliberately out of scope, not overlooked.

OPT-IN, UNSAFE DEFAULT OFF (owner ruling 2026-08-02 s2). The step must name the field: `menu_field` in validate_site_plan's step config. Absent key = today's behaviour byte for byte. Migration 439 sets it on build-site-planner's validate_plan step only.

THE SHARED RESOLVER IS NOT WIDENED, AND THAT IS THE POINT. loadComponentNameResolver has four callers: validate (v3_site_actions.go) and three in apply_gap_plan_action.go (content-gap-planner, 131 dispatches/30d). 407's header and PLAN-049's landmine both record that the gap-planner's menu is DELIBERATELY not widened ('gap-planning a NEW tool page is a different authority ... do not fix the inconsistency without that decision'). Changing the resolver's query or signature would have handed that path the authority an owner-facing decision withheld — silently. The new arm is a method the gap-plan path never calls; the DB query is untouched.

CONSUMERS, ENUMERATED AND TOLD (owner ruling 2026-07-29 s3). Consumers of validate_site_plan, by query over live agent_definitions: build-site-planner.validate_plan (this change) and site-planner.validate_plan (0 rows in orchestration_states; its own menu is section/element-only, so opting it in would add nothing — left untouched, and named in the migration header so the next reader knows it was a decision). content-gap-planner has no validate_site_plan step; it reaches the same Go resolver through apply_gap_plan and its behaviour is unchanged by construction. What changes for a consumer that opts in: validate will no longer delete a section name its own planner step was offered.

ORDER-SAFE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is mandatory on this tree (config is live on apply, Go rides the next roll): migration applied + Go unrolled = the key is unread = today's behaviour; Go rolled + migration unapplied = no menu_field anywhere = today's behaviour.

TESTS ARE MUTATED, NOT MERELY RUN. Nine tests pass; both load-bearing arms were then broken in turn to prove the tests can fail: addMenu made a no-op => MenuFieldKeepsAToolSectionTheBaseWouldDrop fails ('sections = [hero faq], want [hero tool-loan-repayment faq]'); the menu_field gate forced always-on => WithoutMenuFieldTheToolSectionIsStillDropped fails. The second is the one that matters: it proves the opt-in is real, i.e. that no un-opted-in caller's behaviour changed.

CORRECTION TO THE BUG FILE CARRIED IN THIS ROUND. Its ADDENDUM claims a 'SECOND ARM' — a name matching no component survived validate while known tool-level names vanished — and directs the fixing thread to find a branch where an unresolved-name handler discards tool-level rows. No such branch exists: `SELECT component_level FROM content_components WHERE "function"='loans-credit-health-check'` returns component_level='section' (row 824e3309, created 2026-08-13). Arm 1 of resolve() accepts it for the most ordinary reason there is. The simple account — tool-level name, resolve fails, section dropped — is complete.

plan.summary: validate_site_plan gains an opt-in `menu_field` naming the collected-data path holding the component menu its own planner step was shown; those rows are UNIONed into the name resolver's valid set via a new method on the existing resolver, so a widening of the OFFER can never again be silently eaten by the ACCEPTANCE. Config half is migration 439 on build-site-planner only. Closes bugs_open/282; register PLAN-027 amended and related to PLAN-049 in the same commit.

edits.rationale: New file, not a hunk in v3_site_actions.go: that file is edited by several sessions concurrently (it was dirty from another lane this morning) and a same-file passenger cannot be prevented by any pathspec. addMenu UNIONs menu rows into validFunctions/nameToFunc/displayToFunc with the DB base winning on identity collisions; menuRowsFrom refuses anything that is not a non-empty []interface{} so a misconfigured path degrades to today's behaviour rather than to a resolver that accepts ""; resolvedViaMenu exists so a run can SAY the arm fired.

Two minimal hunks. The struct gains menuOnly (attribution only). The call site reads the opt-in key and logs both the arm firing and, per resolved section, whether it owes acceptance to the menu — without that tell, 'the widening reached the plan' and 'the planner proposed nothing from the widened class' are indistinguishable in the logs and in site_plan_sections.

407's idiom: snapshot_agent, jsonb_set, DO-block guard that RAISEs. The guard checks BOTH halves together — menu_field must equal load_components.output_field — because a menu_field naming a path no step writes is the one way this change can be inert while looking applied, which is bugs_open/282 itself one level up. ROLLBACK sidecar removes the key, which is a complete revert whether or not the Go has rolled.

The resolver had ZERO test coverage before this (grep of *_test.go for loadComponentNameResolver: no hits), which is part of why a whole class of names could vanish unnoticed. Nine tests: menu function resolves and is attributed; display-name echo resolves; base identity wins a collision; malformed rows add nothing and never make "" valid; shape variance on the collected-data path; and two sqlmock action-level tests — WITH menu_field the tool section survives, WITHOUT it the identical plan still drops it (the un-opted-in control).
